title: Software Engineering Foundations
description: A preparatory, skills-oriented pathway covering computing, programming, mathematical reasoning, algorithms, and practical software engineering.

completion_policy.note: A recorded pass is provisional learning progress, not proof of mastery or a formally verified skill.

courses.title: Software Engineering Foundations
courses.description: Build the conceptual and practical foundations needed to study and practise software engineering.

modules.title: Computing Foundations
modules.description: Understand how digital information and computer systems work.

lessons.title: Binary, Data, and Representation
lessons.summary: How computers represent numbers, text, and other information.
objectives: Convert small integers between decimal and binary.
Explain bits, bytes, and common units of digital storage.
Describe why text and other data require encoding.

lessons.title: CPU, Memory, Storage, and Operating Systems
lessons.summary: The roles of the processor, memory, persistent storage, and operating system.
objectives: Distinguish CPU, RAM, and persistent storage.
Describe the fetch-decode-execute cycle at a high level.
Explain the role of an operating system and a process.

lessons.title: Command Line and Development Environments
lessons.summary: Navigate files, understand paths, and isolate project dependencies.
objectives: Navigate directories and inspect files with shell commands.
Distinguish absolute and relative paths.
Explain why projects use isolated environments.

modules.title: Programming with Python
modules.description: Learn core programming concepts and express them in readable Python.

lessons.title: Values, Types, Expressions, and Control Flow
lessons.summary: Variables, built-in types, operators, conditions, and loops.
objectives: Use variables and core Python types correctly.
Evaluate expressions and explain type conversions.
Write conditional logic and bounded loops.

lessons.title: Functions, Scope, and Modules
lessons.summary: Decompose problems into reusable functions and organise code.
objectives: Define functions with parameters and return values.
Explain local scope and basic side effects.
Import and organise code into modules.

lessons.title: Collections and Data Modelling
lessons.summary: Use lists, tuples, dictionaries, and sets to represent data.
objectives: Choose an appropriate built-in collection for a task.
Traverse and transform collections.
Explain mutability and common collection operations.

lessons.title: Exceptions, Debugging, and Automated Tests
lessons.summary: Handle errors deliberately and test expected program behaviour.
objectives: Distinguish syntax, runtime, and logic errors.
Use try, except, else, and finally appropriately.
Write tests for normal, boundary, and invalid inputs.

modules.title: Mathematical Reasoning and Algorithms
modules.description: Develop the logical and quantitative reasoning used in programming.

lessons.title: Logic, Sets, Relations, and Functions
lessons.summary: Discrete mathematical language used to describe program behaviour.
objectives: Evaluate basic propositions and logical connectives.
Perform simple set operations.
Explain functions, domains, ranges, and relations.

lessons.title: Algorithmic Thinking and Pseudocode
lessons.summary: Translate a problem into precise, finite steps before coding.
objectives: Identify inputs, outputs, and constraints.
Write structured pseudocode for a small problem.
Trace an algorithm using a hand-worked example.

lessons.title: Algorithm Complexity and Big-O
lessons.summary: Reason about how time and memory requirements grow.
objectives: Distinguish constant, linear, and quadratic growth.
Estimate simple loop complexity.
Compare two approaches using asymptotic reasoning.

lessons.title: Core Data Structures
lessons.summary: Understand arrays/lists, stacks, queues, hash maps, and sets.
objectives: Explain the behaviour of stacks and queues.
Choose between lists, sets, and dictionaries for a task.
Relate data-structure choice to operation costs.

modules.title: Software Engineering Practice
modules.description: Learn the workflow and system concepts used to build dependable software.

lessons.title: Git and Version Control
lessons.summary: Track changes, create branches, and collaborate safely.
objectives: Explain commits, branches, and remotes.
Use status, diff, log, add, commit, and push safely.
Describe how a pull request supports review.

lessons.title: Software Design and Problem Decomposition
lessons.summary: Separate responsibilities and design maintainable components.
objectives: Decompose a small application into responsibilities.
Explain cohesion and coupling in practical terms.
Identify useful module and interface boundaries.

lessons.title: Networking Basics, HTTP, and APIs
lessons.summary: Understand clients, servers, requests, responses, and API contracts.
objectives: Describe client-server communication.
Distinguish common HTTP methods and status-code classes.
Read and construct a simple JSON API request and response.

lessons.title: Relational Databases and SQL Foundations
lessons.summary: Model structured data and query it safely.
objectives: Identify tables, rows, columns, and keys.
Explain primary and foreign keys.
Write basic SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements.

lessons.title: Secure Development Foundations
lessons.summary: Apply basic security thinking to inputs, secrets, and dependencies.
objectives: Explain why inputs must be validated.
Distinguish authentication from authorization.
Describe safe secret handling and dependency updates.
